q: Does a vapour absorption chiller run on waste heat cut emissions compared with an electric chiller?
title: Absorption chiller on waste heat: CO2 gain
short: Yes, when the heat is genuine waste that would otherwise be lost: you save most of the electric chiller's kWh and pay only for pumps and a bigger cooling tower. If a boiler burns fuel to make that heat, a good electric chiller usually emits less: absorption gives only 0.7 to 1.2 units of cooling per unit of heat.
audience: Pharma, food and textile plant engineers

sections.h: Why the heat source decides everything
p: An electric chiller at 0.65 kW per TR delivers about 5.4 units of cooling per unit of electricity (3.517 / 0.65). A vapour absorption machine (VAM) delivers about 0.65 to 0.7 units of cooling per unit of heat in a single effect machine and about 1.2 in a double effect one, which needs higher grade heat (CIBSE Datasheet 7, absorption cooling). That trade only pays in CO2 when the heat costs no extra fuel: DG or gas engine jacket water and exhaust, excess low pressure steam, hot condensate or process waste heat.

sections.h: The test for genuine waste heat
ul: The heat was being vented, dumped to a cooling tower or lost before the VAM came in.
No boiler fires harder because of the VAM, in any season.
If the waste heat runs short and a backup burner tops it up, that fuel counts against the VAM.
The cooling tower rejects the cooling load plus the driving heat, so a VAM needs a larger tower, more pump power and more make-up water than an electric chiller of the same TR.
Solution pumps and vacuum pumps draw a few kW.
Part load COP falls, and a VAM needs steady heat to hold its rating.

p: Electricity avoided lowers location-based Scope 2 at 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh. Any fuel burned for the VAM is Scope 1. Report both lines rather than a single net saving, so a reviewer can see the heat source assumption.

example.title: Illustrative example: 200 TR for 5,000 hours (1,000,000 TR hours)
lines: Electric chiller at 0.65 kW per TR: 650,000 kWh; CO2: 650,000 x 0.710 = 461,500 kg
VAM auxiliaries, pumps and extra tower power at 0.15 kW per TR (assumed): 150,000 kWh; CO2: 106,500 kg
On genuine waste heat: saving = 461,500 minus 106,500 = 355,000 kg, about 355 t a year
On heat from a furnace oil boiler: cooling 1,000,000 x 3.517 = 3,517,000 kWh; heat at COP 1.2 = 2,930,833 kWh; fuel at 85% boiler efficiency = 3,448,039 kWh = 12.41 TJ
Fuel CO2 at 77.4 t per TJ (IPCC default, residual fuel oil): 12.41 x 77.4 = 961 t, plus 106.5 t for auxiliaries, against 461.5 t for the electric chiller
example.note: kW per TR, COP and boiler efficiency are assumptions; use your data sheets and measured hours.

senseible: Senseible reads electricity and fuel bills into one monthly record, so the shift from chiller kWh to heat, and any extra fuel, shows on the same page.
